scope: Standalone pixel-flipping input precision and CSV coordinates/baselines
confirmed_regression: A real float64 linear model failed in Quantus PixelFlipping because numpy inputs were converted to default float32 tensors before prediction.
coverage: Real Quantus PixelFlipping executes with float32 and float64 models
Every perturbed input equals an independently constructed reference tensor, including information representable only in float64
Finite prediction curves equal direct reference-model predictions
Cached NPZ image and attribution files pass through the complete standalone CSV export path
Original model precision and global torch default precision remain unchanged
CSV drops use a separately evaluated original-image score; unavailable baseline values remain NaN
Curve return arrays and their sample counts remain post-perturbation samples
Coordinates use explicit feature count and step size, with a partial last step clipped to 100 percent
A writer fixture with 36 features and step size 5 starts at 13.88888888888889 percent, ends at 100 percent and rejects the incorrect seven-row curve
Unknown feature geometry remains NaN instead of inventing coordinates

impact.historical_data: No historical cached curves, scores or published results were recomputed or relabeled
impact.separate_scoring_path: QuantusEvaluator score extraction and its CSV writer are handled by the separate metric validation task

limitations: Synthetic CPU inputs and a small linear model validate the repaired path; they do not reproduce the published experiment
The nondivisible writer case is tested independently because the installed Quantus metric rejects nondivisible spatial step sizes before evaluation
